checkKinds.subject: Locate one paper-facts subject by `entity`, then apply: typesInclude / typesExclude (history + active concrete pointer types, whitespace-normalised), bucket / bucketPrefix (coverage_ledger.py bucket), callbackStateNotIn, fields (dotted path inside the subject row -> required value; a list value means 'contains all').
checkKinds.noFeature: The report's featureDiagnostics must contain no `unsupported` record with one of these feature names.

gates.title: Every lost pointer names where and why it was lost
Constant function-pointer array call expands to its initialiser targets
ops-table call through a pointer base resolves by (record type, field)
Table-driven state machine: array-of-struct fptr field resolves to all states
Callback stored in a global resolves at the later invocation site
Global function pointer reassigned elsewhere: initializer is not the whole target set
Context stored in a global inherits the interpretation made after the later load
Payload stored in a heap struct in one function, interpreted after a load in another
Write one union member, read another: a cast with no CastExpr
Tagged union: discriminant-guarded parallel interpretations of shared storage
Modelled library functions forward data into project callbacks
Modelled library functions copy / return-alias pointer values
dlsym literal links to the project definition; non-literal is an explicit boundary

P0.title: Escape accounting
reviewQuestions: For each sampled subject: is the pointer really passed to the named callee at the cited line?
Sites of kind `project`: is the callee really a project function defined in another TU (so the loss is a cross-TU summary that contributed nothing, not external code)?
Is every named callee truly outside the analysed project (no body in any analysed TU)?
Does any sampled subject look lost for a reason the record does not mention?
Indirect call sites: do the calleeExprKind labels match the source expression?
Is the corpus (corpus.json) representative enough to steer P1 and P4, or should projects be added?
agentNotes: Scope: reporting only. P0 adds `subject.escape` and `indirectCallSites` to paper facts (schema v10) and `indirectCallSites` to the report. No analysis path reads them.

Equivalence check: all 87 `examples/*.c` plus the 11 original fixtures were run with the pre-P0 and final P0 builds (text output, link summary, report, paper facts = 384 files). After removing the two new fields and the version number, every file is byte-identical / JSON-equal.

`escape` is evidence, not a verdict. A subject can be typed and still escape (it is then bucketed `resolved`). `reasons` lists every reason; `reason` is the first. Each site has a kind: `external`, `project`, `indirect-external` or `indirect`.

Self-review of the first packet found three accounting errors, now fixed and covered by fixture checks: (1) 87 of 950 corpus escapes said `external-unmodeled` with no callee. They were arguments to project functions in other TUs, which the pre-existing `externalBoundary` flag treats as external because it consults only the current TU. These are now `forwarded-to-project` with the callee named (`escape_cross_tu/`). (2) Indirect calls whose target is known but external (parson `parson_free` = `free`) were reported as unresolved callbacks; they are now `external-unmodeled` via `free`, site kind `indirect-external` (`ext_indirect_external.c`). (3) zlib `inflateBack::in_desc` was blocked with no reason; added `callback-formal` (`ext_formal_callback.c`).

Existing soundness gap, not fixed in P0: a global function pointer is resolved from its initializer only, and reassignments in other functions are ignored (parson: `parson_free = free`, reassigned at parson.c:2053). P0 labels these sites `global-initializer`, not `flow-sensitive`, and adds the red gate `P1-fp-global-reassigned`, so P1 must fix it.

Known limitation: escape sites inside macros point at the macro's spelling location (binn: `#define strnicmp strncasecmp`). The tool's `sourceSpan` uses spelling locations everywhere; switching to expansion locations would change every output, so it should be its own change.
Library functions the tool already treats as memory/string sinks (`memcpy`, `strlen`, ...) have their own pointer-use kind and are not recorded as escapes. Revisit in P4.

Corpus limits: lua-5.4.1 is excluded by default because `build_summary_index.py` needs more than 25 minutes on its 94 MB of summaries (a pre-existing problem, worth fixing before P1, since lua is the richest function-pointer project). vsftpd `sysdeputil.c` needs PAM headers that are not installed here. thttpd needs configure-equivalent defines and two generated headers, which are in `corpus-include/`.

Pre-existing, not P0: `validate_paper_facts.py` rejects hiredis `test.c` for a duplicate `declarationId` (`sds.h:89:44`, an inline function in a header). The pre-P0 build produces the same error. All other corpus and fixture paper facts validate.

P1.title: Function-value slots
reviewQuestions: For each sampled call site: is every listed target really storable in that slot? (precision)
Can you find a function that can reach the site but is missing from the targets? (recall)
Do the new parallel histories on data arguments read as true alternatives, not artefacts?
Did any subject's classification move toward wild-like without a real second target?

P2.title: Data slots
reviewQuestions: For each sampled subject: does the inherited type come from a load of the same field/global?
Are generic containers reported as polymorphic carriers rather than resolved to one type?
Did any previously precise instance-keyed result get widened by the type-keyed slot?

P3.title: Unions
reviewQuestions: For each sampled pun: are the written and read members really different views of the same object?
For each tagged union: is the reported discriminant the field the code actually tests?
Are unions the model cannot handle reported as unsupported rather than silently skipped?

P4.title: External contracts
reviewQuestions: Does each contract match the documented behaviour of the library function?
Were the modelled callees chosen from the top of the P0 escape-callee ranking?
For each sampled subject: is the type it gained really reached through the modelled call?

P5.title: Dynamic loading
reviewQuestions: Is each name-matched dlsym binding the definition a real loader would find?
Are non-literal symbol lookups reported as dynamic-symbol boundaries?
